questions.instruction: Read two sentences below and choose the best way of combining them.
questions.passage: Lisa plays the piano. Her sister Kelly plays the piano too.
questions.prompt: Which is the best way of combining the sentences?

options.A: Lisa and her sister Kelly plays the piano.
options.B: Both Lisa and her sister Kelly play the piano.
options.C: Lisa plays the piano, and Kelly plays the piano.
options.D: Lisa and Kelly too play the piano.

questions.instruction: Read two sentences below and choose the best way of combining them.
questions.passage: Kazuko took her dog for a walk. They went to the park.
questions.prompt: Which is the best way of combining the sentences?

options.A: Kazuko, going to the park, took her dog for a walk.
options.B: Kazuko took her dog for a walk to the park.
options.C: Kazuko took her dog for a walk because they went to the park.
options.D: Kazuko and her dog went to the park, where she and the dog walked.

questions.instruction: Read two sentences below and choose the best way of combining them.
questions.passage: We knew it might get chilly at the football game. We brought along some extra blankets.
questions.prompt: Which is the best way of combining the sentences?

options.A: We knew it might get chilly at the football game when we brought along some extra blankets.
options.B: Bringing along some extra blankets, we knew it might get chilly at the football game.
options.C: We brought along some extra blankets because we knew it might get chilly at the football game.
options.D: It got chilly at the football game, and we brought along some extra blankets.

questions.instruction: Read some texts and find the right answers
questions.passage: Television has been introduced to almost every country in the world, reaching a large number of viewers on every continent. About 600 million people saw the first person walk on the moon, and a billion people watched the twentieth Olympic Games. Television has in many ways promoted understanding and cooperation among people. It does this by showing educational and cultural programs.
questions.prompt: From this passage, a reader can most reasonably conclude that the author believes that

options.A: people spend too much time watching television
options.B: not every country needs to have television
options.C: television can unify people from around the world
options.D: television is as important as schools

questions.instruction: Read some texts and find the right answers
questions.passage: People have different ways of learning. Some are better at making mental pictures of new ideas. Others are more comfortable with writing lists of things to memorize. Certain people can learn best when listening to music, while others need silence to concentrate.
questions.prompt: Which of the following is the main idea of the passage?

options.A: Mental pictures help many to learn.
options.B: Some people prefer lists to making mental pictures.
options.C: To learn well you need to be comfortable.
options.D: Different individuals have different ways of acquiring information.

questions.instruction: Read some texts and find the right answers
questions.passage: If you hold a piece of copper wire over the flame of a wooden match, heat will be conducted by the copper wire to your fingers, and you will be forced to drop the wire. You will, however, still be able to hold the match because wood is a poor conductor of heat.
questions.prompt: Which of the following is implied in the passage above?

options.A: Copper is a good conductor of heat.
options.B: Wood and copper conduct heat equally.
options.C: Wood is an excellent conductor of heat.
options.D: Matches should be made of copper.
